title: Banded cascade trace analysis and remediation notes
summary: Exploratory notes from a banded / cascade-style trace analysis. Goal: isolate p95/p99 contributors across sequence-length bands and batch sizes, validate hypothesized KV/cache and memcpy hot spots, and propose low-risk mitigations.
content:
Context:
This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation into recent p95/p99 regressions observed on the hosted inference fleet (route: text-gen-chat). Rather than a single aggregate view, we "banded" traces by sequence-length buckets and then examined the stage cascade (queue -> preprocess -> kv/cache -> attention/kernels -> postprocess -> egress). The banded-cascade approach surfaced stage shifts that were invisible in the overall waterfall.

Trace collection / sampling notes:
- Traces collected via OTEL agent + custom span tags (route, seqlen, batch_size, model_variant). Sampling: reservoir sampling at collector with bias toward head-of-queue errors (sample rate roughly 1/200 requests, increased to 1/50 during repro window).
- Correlated traces with GPU perf counters (ncu export) using trace_id mapping. Also pulled host-level iostat and numa stats for nodes that showed high p99.
- Aggregate tool: tools/trace_aggregate.py (args: --group-by seqlen_bin,batch_size,stage --metric latency_ms --quantiles 50,95,99).

Definitions / stage boundaries used in this analysis:
- request-queueing: time in request router before being scheduled to a worker.
- tokenization: tokenizer.exec (including model-specific tokenization).
- kv-prepare: prefix lookup + KV cache query + host->device prefetch (if enabled).
- attention-kernel: dominant GPU kernels (matmul/attention with fused softmax paths).
- memcpy: host<->device memcpy (includes pinned buffer allocation time when applicable).
- serialization-egress: JSON marshaling and network write.

High-level aggregated numbers (all traces sampled, mixed batch sizes):
- overall p50: 42 ms
- overall p95: 172 ms
- overall p99: 412 ms

But these numbers hide significant heterogeneity. Key banded results (examples):
1) Short seq (<=64), batch_size=1:
  - p50: 30 ms, p95: 84 ms, p99: 120 ms
  - dominant stage at p99: request-queueing (40%) + memcpy (20%)
2) Medium seq (65-512), batch_size=1:
  - p50: 60 ms, p95: 210 ms, p99: 360 ms
  - dominant stage at p99: attention-kernel (45%), kv-prepare (20%)
3) Long seq (>512), batch_size=1:
  - p50: 180 ms, p95: 540 ms, p99: 920 ms
  - dominant stage at p99: attention-kernel (60%), memcpy (15%)
4) Batch size effects (seqlen bucket 65-512):
  - batch=1 p99: 360 ms (as above)
  - batch=4 p99: 240 ms (queue wait + amortized kernel cost lower)
  - batch=8 p99: 300 ms (queue wait spikes for tail requests; increased serialization contention visible)

Coldstart vs warm:
- coldstart window (first request on a freshly started worker) p99 observed ~670 ms. Warm steady-state worker p99 ~412 ms. Main coldstart contributors: driver/kernel JIT and allocator pin overhead for first memcpy.

Key observations and hypotheses (ranked):
1) Attention kernel dominates for high seqlen p99: attention kernel time scales superlinearly with seq length in our fused implementation; large memory working sets also increase L2 cache churn resulting in longer kernel durations. Reproduced locally on A100 with nvprof.
2) KV cache path shows amplified latency in medium seq band for certain routes: hot prefixes with many small keys cause many host-level hashmap lookups, occasionally triggering host-side locking and scatter prefetches. This increases kv-prepare and also causes jitter in memcpy timing due to late prefetch.
3) Memcpy overhead is non-trivial for many p99s, especially when using non-pinned allocations in the trace window. Observed a burst of pinned-alloc overhead when worker pools scale up (allocator hit path).
4) Batching reduces amortized kernel time per request but shifts the tail to queue-wait when traffic is spiky; naive large batch thresholds increase p99 for latency-sensitive routes.
5) GPU utilization is sublinear: many traces show <45% SM utilization during long-kernel spans (kernel launch serialization and small op fragments); suggests kernel launch overhead and missing kernel fusion.

Root-cause experiments run so far:
- A: Disabled device-prefetch for KV to measure host->device memcpy contribution: total p99 dropped ~45 ms across medium/long bands, but kv-prepare p95 rose (CPU cost moved back).
- B: Forced pinned buffer reuse (arena allocator) on a subset of workers: memcpy variance decreased, p99 improved ~30 ms for short seq traces.
- C: Upgraded a small fleet to H100 (same config): attention kernel median dropped ~1.7x, p99 improved ~210 ms for long seq band (not a full solution — cost and availability concerns).
- D: Increased batching threshold from 8->16 on non-latency critical routes: headroom increased, but p99 for latency routes increased due to queueing spillover.

Actionable mitigations (fast follow):
1) Deploy pinned buffer arena by default to reduce first-touch pinned allocation overhead. Owner: Jordan Park. ETA: 1 week for pilot.
2) Implement selective device-resident KV for hot-prefixes: a small LRU cache kept on-device for prefixes above a hit-rate threshold. Prototype required to measure memory tradeoffs. Owner: Eleni Petrov. ETA: 3 weeks for prototype.
3) Dynamic batcher throttles keyed by seqlen band: smaller max batch for seqlen>512, allow larger batch on seqlen<=64. Implemented asPolicy in router config. Owner: Samir Patel. ETA: 2 weeks.
4) Kernel fusion experiment: try cublasLt kernel variants and test fused attention kernels + persistent streams to reduce kernel launch stalls. Owner: Research/Applied-ML. ETA: spike 2 weeks.
5) Improve trace instrumentation to capture allocator/pinned-alloc spans explicitly (helps confirm allocator overhead). Owner: Maya. ETA: 3 days.

Open questions / risks:
- How many active prefixes are 'hot' enough to justify device-resident KV? Memory budget on GPU is limited; need a small working set estimate.
- Will pinned arena interfere with multi-tenant memory accounting? Need SRE/infra input.
- Kernel fusion risk: correctness regressions on quantized kernels; need model-specific verification and perf guardrails.

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- Run trace_aggregate for each model_variant separately and check if quantized variants move p99 differently.
- Add allocator/pinned-alloc span tags (heap_id, reuse_count).
- Correlate p99 nodes with host-level iostat/numastat — we saw a couple nodes with high remote NUMA reads.
- Follow up PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/893 (pin-arena prototype)

Appendix: sample commands used during the investigation
- python tools/trace_aggregate.py --input traces/2026-02-25/*.json --group-by seqlen_bin,batch_size,stage --quantiles 50,95,99 --out summary/2026-02-25.json
- otel-collector config: sampling.rate=1/200 (in the repro experiment increased to 1/50)
- ncu --target-processes all --set full --export traces/ncu/trace_20260225.ncu

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Add allocator/pinned span (Maya) and deploy to canary fleet.
- Start pinned arena pilot (Jordan) on 10% workers. Gather 48h p95/p99 delta.
- Kick off device-KV prototype design doc (Eleni) and collect hot-prefix histogram (via trace tags) to size device cache.

If reviewers: please call out any missing instrumentation that would make bands more actionable (e.g., per-stage GPU-mem footprint, CUDA stream concurrency).
